Hi Ava — great to hear. Quick answers and I'll follow up with an ops-level playbook this afternoon.

1) Burst envelope: we propose a two-tier model: a committed slab (reserved GPUs) that covers the SLA-backed baseline, and a billable shoulder lane called the "safeguard pool" for short bursts. Billable shoulder usage is invoiced daily with minute-granularity; billing rates are lower than on-demand but higher than committed. I'll include a worked example in the spreadsheet.

2) Autoscale safety: Redwood supports deterministic priority tags. We can map your workloads into three priority classes: P0 (real-time agents), P1 (nearline feature ingestion), P2 (batch jobs). In outage scenarios we perform preemptive spillover from P2 -> P1 -> P0 with optional pre-warming of P0 slices in secondary regions.

3) Auditability: we provide an incident bundle with token-level trace, per-node CPU/GPU utilization, queue latencies, and the exact scaling decisions (time, reason, affected job ids). Those are surfaced in the Console and exported as a daily incident artifact.

Attaching a draft burst matrix (xlsx) and an ops summary. Will also propose simple SLA language for the addendum.

Cheers,
Ben

Thanks — read and polished. Here are the operational commits I'm comfortable with for the proposal: 

- Committed slab: size will be set to cover 95th-percentile steady-state QPS over a 30-day window (customer-supplied profile).
- Safeguard pool (shoulder): default = 18% of committed slab, billable per-minute with daily aggregation; we will include a worked example in the addendum. Option to increase to 30% as a priced uplift.
- Pre-warm policy: for P0 we offer a one-time pre-warm credit equal to 6 hours in a secondary region for onboarding; after that, pre-warm is charged per-minute.
- Eviction & fallback: P2 jobs will be preempted first; P1 can be throttled before P0 is touched. In cross-region failover we will attempt pre-warm within 30 minutes; if unsuccessful, we will route P0 to the hosted fallback profile with degraded latency SLO (documented in addendum).
- Incident artifact: daily incident bundle containing scaling events (timestamp, reason code), per-request trace ids for affected sessions, and a CSV of token-level latencies. Bundle retained for 90 days by default; 1-year retention is available as an add-on.

Monica — I left placeholders in the matrix for the pricing delta. Laura — draft the short clause below for the addendum and I'll iterate. Ava/Jordan — if this matches your expectation I'll generate the DocuSign packet with the autoscale addendum and the worked example invoice.

Proposed addendum clause (draft): "Billable Burst: Customer is allocated a Safeguard Pool equal to 18% of the committed GPU slab by default. Usage of the Safeguard Pool is billed per-minute and aggregated daily. In the event of sustained usage beyond the Safeguard Pool for more than 6 hours, Redwood will engage capacity planning to offer either a temporary commitment uplift or recommend burst credits to avoid disruption."

I'll attach the revised matrix and a DocuSign link in the next email.

- Karthik
